PUBLIC DFT TABLES · GREAT BRITAIN

What factors are being recorded?

Published motorcycle summaries, with the two recording systems kept separate.

Assessed contributing circumstances, not proven causes. Multiple factors can apply. These figures cover police-attended collisions with at least one factor recorded, not all motorcycle collisions or all riding.

Factors assigned to motorcycles

Source: DfT RAS0702. The unit is a motorcycle involved in a collision, not an injured person. Severity refers to the collision, which may involve injury to someone else. The denominator includes motorcycles with no factor assigned to them when another participant has a factor.

Loading published tables…

Two methods, shown separately

Converted CFs are older contributory-factor records mapped into RSF categories. Direct RSFs were recorded using the new system. These groups differ in police-force coverage and potentially collision mix. A gap between columns is not an estimate of the effect of changing systems, or evidence of a change in causes.

DfT numbers and percentages are independently rounded; adjusted counts are estimates. Zero percent can reflect rounding. Missing values remain unavailable. Rows overlap and must not be added. Individual factors are ranked by direct percentage when available, otherwise converted percentage. Group subtotals are excluded.

Follow a factor without joining the series

The columns retain the recording break. Even within one method, contributing forces change over time. Small early direct-RSF samples are particularly unstable. No statistical test of a recording-system effect is made here.

The collision context is a different question

RAS0701 asks which factors occurred anywhere in the collisions in which motorcycle users were injured. It includes riders and passengers and may include a factor assigned to another driver. It is not a measure of rider error.

Fixed example: 2025, directly recorded RSFs, adjusted KSI. The controls above do not change it.

What the new assignment split adds

The September 2026 RAS0701 split table reports ineffective observation in 53% of its eligible motorcycle-user adjusted KSI casualties when considering any participant, and 52% where assigned to a driver or rider. “Driver or rider” can include someone driving another vehicle; this does not isolate the motorcyclist. Categories overlap. DfT recoded some erroneous assignments for this table, so it can differ from other factor products.

What this means for research

These summaries support investigating observation, manoeuvring, experience, speed and braking. They do not measure reaction time, brake pressure, returning-rider status or exposure to advice. The age × capacity × participant-factor combinations still require detailed access.

The RSF label “too fast for conditions” includes loss of control or swerving and is distinct from exceeding the speed limit. A low recorded braking percentage does not show that braking is unimportant: assessment, coverage and category definitions affect what is recorded.
